PLANNING TASK -- WRITE A FIX PLAN FOR SIX REVIEW FINDINGS ON PR #807 (the read-only production disk inventory) AND CHANGE NOTHING ELSE. Create exactly ONE new file, codex-plans/disk-inventory-r6-fixes-plan.md, containing your complete answer in Markdown. Do not modify, create or delete any other file in this repository, and do not implement any fix. Avoid trailing whitespace. Do not contact production. Do NOT check out or switch to any other commit: the working tree must stay on the implementation branch the wrapper created. Instead run `git fetch origin codex/run-38130707546-1` and read files at commit 396439c23eca424329d8e4da25dcea5e28713ae2 with `git show 396439c23eca424329d8e4da25dcea5e28713ae2:<path>`. If you want to run tests at that commit, create a temporary git worktree OUTSIDE the repository directory (for example under /tmp), run them there, and remove the worktree before you finish. If that commit is not reachable after the fetch, say so in the file and stop. Every section below is part of the file's content.

FILES: scripts/operator/actions/v3-disk-inventory.sh (a bash launcher with an embedded CPython 3.14 program); tests/test_v3_disk_inventory.py (88 tests -- many assert on the LITERAL SOURCE TEXT of the action through `in source`, and some are negative assertions that record wrong implementations which must never come back); docs/operations/v3-finder-production-rollout-state.md. Also read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml (the action runs inside the shared `execute` job, timeout-minutes 40).

THE SIX FINDINGS, AS THE REVIEWER WROTE THEM (line numbers are at 396439c):

[F1, line 710] Reserve closing scans against the global deadline. "When the pre-closing walk approaches its 1,200-second allowance, this global limit reserves only 240 seconds for post-scan SQL, not the 900 seconds required by the three independently budgeted closing scans. Even with no intervening SQL, only 360 seconds remain under the 1,800-second action deadline, so the PGDATA scan can consume 300 seconds and starve the mandatory WAL scan and base scan despite each remaining within its configured allowance. begin_closing_scan() resets only the scan-local deadline and cannot restore global time; deduct the remaining closing-scan reserve from overall while the walk is active."

[F2, line 513] Resolve bind aliases against non-mount source paths. "When a normal directory such as /var/lib/data is bind-mounted at another path below usage_root, /proc/mounts contributes the bind target but the original directory is not itself a mount point, so it is never added to points. Grouping only mount-point targets by (st_dev, st_ino) therefore cannot form an alias pair for the usual bind-mount layout; the root du -x still traverses both paths, while the negative df/du residual can offset the duplicate and leave a successful closed receipt. Resolve each bind mount's underlying source/root or fail closed when it cannot be deduplicated."

[F3, line 2395] Do not infer WAL stability from equal byte totals. "When WAL grows during the directory scan and is recycled back to the same byte total before the second SQL read, these endpoint values compare equal even though the scan may have observed the transiently larger directory. Equality of two aggregate sizes does not establish one stable snapshot -- fixed-size WAL recycling can readily return to the same total -- so the excess becomes an 'unlisted' reclaim candidate and the walk-to-SQL adjustment can still make the partition close successfully. Treat equal totals as insufficient proof of stability, or avoid classifying this difference as reclaimable."

[F4, line 3127] Carry the skipped WAL walk-to-scan adjustment. "When the two SQL WAL readings differ and the earlier PGDATA walk also measured a different size from the dedicated WAL scan, this branch records only wal_dir_bytes_at_sql - wal_bytes_after_scan and then continue skips the later walk_figure - wal_dir_bytes_at_sql adjustment. The candidate identity therefore remains short by that second delta, causing candidates_partition_unaccounted_at_scan to be false and the otherwise valid inventory to stop during ordinary WAL churn; append both signed differences, or directly reconcile the PGDATA-walk figure to the closing SQL figure."

[F5, line 1676] Sort slots with unknown WAL status after retaining slots. "When more than 50 slots include enough unused physical slots whose WAL has never been reserved, wal_status is NULL, making both leading sort expressions NULL; PostgreSQL 18 emits that null status for an invalid/unreserved restart_lsn, and descending order defaults to NULLS FIRST. Those non-retaining slots can therefore fill the bounded sample ahead of every extended or reserved slot and hide the slots actually explaining disk usage; add NULLS LAST to both status expressions or coalesce them to false."

[F6, line 1351] Report truncation of the root directory scan. "When the depth-2 filesystem walk emits more than 4,000 records, calling du_rows() here discards the omitted-record count and byte total returned by du_stream(). exclusive_usage() then folds every omitted descendant into its nearest retained ancestor -- potentially / or /var -- so the arithmetic still closes while the receipt attributes a large aggregate to that ancestor and provides no indication that thousands of actual paths were removed by the cap. Use du_stream() directly and expose or conservatively classify the omitted aggregate instead of presenting the retained paths as a complete location partition."

FOR EACH FINDING ANSWER: (a) is it correct at 396439c -- verify against the code and say exactly why or why not, including whether any consequence it describes refers to behaviour or fields that no longer exist at this commit; (b) the root cause; (c) the fix, precise enough to implement (functions, lines, constants added or removed, receipt fields), and whether a better fix REMOVES behaviour rather than adding it; (d) every test in tests/test_v3_disk_inventory.py that pins the affected source text or behaviour, and how it must change while keeping each test's behavioural subject and every negative assertion; (e) what the fix could plausibly break, or what the next review round would most likely find in it.

THEN, ACROSS ALL SIX: whether the findings share a cause; the order to apply the fixes and every interaction between them (for example a fix that frees or consumes scan budget relevant to F1); and a final arithmetic check of the action's time budget after your fixes -- walk, closing scans and SQL against ACTION_BUDGET_SECONDS and the 40-minute job -- stating the time each phase is guaranteed. Cite file:line for every claim and mark assumptions as assumptions.
